items.en: The NTDA’s 12th Tyre Industry Conference in Birmingham, themed ‘The Tyre Professional’, featured particularly pertinent presentations from Halfords’ Rich Bruce and Michelin’s Matthew Ireson, Speaking from the tyre retail and manufacturer perspectives respectively, they set out complementary views on what professionalism means in a changing market. Bruce, a relative newcomer to the sector, argued that the scale of the task – 40 million vehicles requiring safe, correctly recommended tyres – combined with rapid technical complexity (TPMS, alignment, ADAS) already makes every technician a professional. Ireson, drawing on a personal account of his elderly parents relying on a competent local fitter, positioned the tyre professional as a translator who turns engineering into clear customer confidence.

Meanwhile, both agreed that the growing up-take of online pre-sale research amongst consumers, combined with the rise of AI-powered search means consumers need a simple “reason-to-believe” narrative to combat the complexity of the proliferation of brands, products and technologies associated with tyre-buying.
“50 per cent of consumers are already using AI-powered search to guide them through their entire choices” – Matthew Ireson, Michelin Category Manager, Europe North Region

For his part, Matthew Ireson, Michelin, Category Manager, Europe North Region exemplified the approach he espouses by telling the real-life story of an occasion when his elderly parents needed to change their tyres:

“Their car is literally their lifeline. Without it, they’d be completely lost…So [Ireson’s mother] went straight to her local garage and [saw]…her tyre professional…He fitted them a nice set of premium tyres…they’re back on the road and all was good.”
Halfords, Garage Commercial and Fleet Director, Rich Bruce addressed the question of whether or not tyre technicians are already professionals and was emphatic in his affirmation that they are:

“Yes, absolutely. There’s 40 million vehicles on the road, each of them having tyres that need to be recommended to them, and each of them having tyres that need to be fitted safely. So yes, that responsibility is great. And as such, I think we should be seeing each and every one of those technicians as a professional.”

Kwik Fit recent held its annual Tyre Insight Day for the fleet industry, with this year’s event reportedly the biggest yet. In order to accommodate additional requests from customers Kwik Fit broadened the content and moved the event to Mercedes-Benz World, on the site of the historic Brooklands racing circuit. The day’s programme included insights from across Kwik Fit’s parent group, European Tyre Enterprise Limited (ETEL), as well as from Continental, one of the company’s strategic tyre partners.
An as yet unknown number of Peugeot 3008 and 5008 cars have received a recall notice due to faulty tyre labelling.

A 21 October EU Safety Gate announcement (OR/00115/26) notes that Peugeot 3008 V3 and 5008 V3 cars feature some vehicles “registered with class A+ tyres, while the tyres actually fitted are class B. Therefore, the CO₂ emissions declared in the certificate of conformity, which are related to the tyre class, are incorrect.”
As a result, effective 1 July 2026, the car manufacturer issued a “recall of the product from end users”.

MobileIT @pps is extending the payment gateway on TiDaeX with a new transaction-based model to enable users to be plugged into connected parties such as dealers, breakdown services and manufacturers beyond standard e-jobsheet functionality via TiDaeX. The goal is to provide “visible and transparent data between connected parties”. And the upgrade is expected to break cover in 2027.
